fix_commit_message:
avcodec/vvc/refs: Check content_ref in set_pict_type()

Fixes: 390565846/clusterfuzz-testcase-minimized-ffmpeg_AV_CODEC_ID_VVC_fuzzer-4990028521996288
Fixes: Null pointer dereference

Found-by: continuous fuzzing process https://github.com/google/oss-fuzz/tree/master/projects/ffmpeg
Signed-off-by: Michael Niedermayer <michael@niedermayer.cc>
agent_reasoning: Merged diff composed mechanically by cherry-picking fix a50d36b5fd39 on top of intro 8eb1d76e146a via git's 3-way merge. Vulnerability (NullPointerDereference): The VVC decoder's set_pict_type() function, added to export a frame's picture type (I/P/B) and keyframe flag, scans the current access unit's coded bitstream (CBS) units for slice NAL units and inspects their parsed slice header (content_ref) to determine whether the frame contains inter or B slices. The loop only checked unit->type against VVC_RSV_IRAP_11 but did not verify that unit->content_ref was actually non-NULL before dereferencing it as an H266RawSliceHeader pointer within the IS_I/IS_B macros. Malformed input can produce a unit with a slice-type NAL unit type but a NULL content_ref, leading to a crash. Root cause: Missing NULL check on unit->content_ref before dereferencing it as a parsed slice header structure; the code assumed that any CBS unit with a slice-like NAL unit type would always have its content_ref populated, which is not guaranteed for malformed/incompletely parsed bitstreams.
